title: Bolton ghost hunters' eerie night inside one of UK's 'most haunted' hotels
excerpt: A mysterious breath, a fallen doll and footsteps outside an empty room were among the eerie encounters reported by Bolton ghost hunters during a…
content:
A mysterious breath, a fallen doll and footsteps outside an empty room were among the eerie encounters reported by Bolton ghost hunters during a night inside a "haunted" hotel.

Para-Northern's Emma Flood and Lorna Hartley spent the night at Ye Olde Kings Head in Chester after years of wanting to investigate the centuries-old building.

Emma and Lorna (Image: Emma Flood)

The pair previously told The Bolton News they were hoping for a scary night – and while Emma admits much of their stay was surprisingly quiet, there were a few moments which left them searching for an explanation.

Ye Olde Kings Head, on Lower Bridge Street, has become renowned for its ghost stories and is home to My Haunted Hotel, where visitors investigate the building before spending the night there.

(Image: Emma Flood)

Cameras monitor the hotel around the clock, meaning unusual sights and sounds can be checked from a control room.

One of the first things to catch Emma's attention was what sounded like a man breathing in one of the rooms.

She said: "I did hear a breath in one of the rooms.

"The hotel has got 24-hour surveillance cameras filming all the time and you can ring through on the walkie-talkie to the control room.

"He checked and he could hear it."

There were other people nearby and Emma said she considered whether the noise could have come from one of them.

However, she said nobody appeared to be doing anything which would explain the loud breath.

Things became stranger when the group moved into an area associated with stories of the building's past as a brothel.

A sudden bang came from the floor above.

Emma said: "We were all in the brothel area and went, 'What the hell was that? What's above us?'

"They said, 'That's room five, where all the dolls are.'"

When the group went upstairs, one of the dolls had fallen over.

(Image: Emma Flood)

Emma and the others tried jumping around near it to see whether vibrations or movement could cause it to fall again – but it stayed put.

She said: "There's no way around it, it just falls.

"We stood in front of her and jumped up and down and she wouldn't move."

(Image: Emma Flood)

Emma and Lorna later settled down for the night in room three – and there was one feature which immediately made them uneasy.

The bedroom was filled with mirrors.

Emma said she and Lorna avoid having mirrors in bedrooms because of a paranormal belief that they can act as "portals", particularly while people are asleep and at their most vulnerable.

(Image: Emma Flood)

She said: "You shouldn't have mirrors in your bedroom.

"When you're asleep you're at your most vulnerable, so you've got to be very careful."

Nevertheless, the pair put in their earplugs and went to sleep.

At around 4.30am, Lorna woke to discover a torch had fallen over.

Emma said: "Realistically, she may have moved it in her sleep, so we can't say for definite.

"We're still waiting for them to look at the footage."

The following morning, after the other visitors had left, Emma and Lorna carried out another investigation.

They headed into room six, where a rocking chair sits inside a pentagram on the floor.

(Image: Emma Flood)

The room is associated with stories of a woman named Heidi who is said to have fallen to her death from a window.

Emma and Lorna began asking questions and said they were met by footsteps, creaking floorboards, knocks and taps.

Emma said: "We started getting responses – footsteps, creaking, knocks and taps in the room."

Yet despite Ye Olde Kings Head's reputation, Emma described the night as relatively quiet overall.

(Image: Emma Flood)

And with spooky season around the corner, the Chester hotel is far from the only building which has left the Bolton investigators with questions.

One experience which Emma recently visited was an old mill off Cherry Tree Lane in Bury, dating back to 1876.

Para-Northern was invited to investigate the building before it was sold – and Emma's verdict on that night was simple.

She said: "That was just insane."

The team reported hearing what sounded like a woman's voice, bangs around machinery which had not been touched for months and, at one point, somebody apparently whistling.

In the boardroom, the group also repeatedly heard what sounded like knocks on a table.

One person was taking part in the Estes Method, where an investigator wears headphones and listens for potential responses without being able to hear what the rest of the group is saying.

Emma said: "He even took his headphones off and said, 'Is someone banging on the table?'"

Things did not get any less unsettling when they ventured into the cellar.

Emma said motion sensor lights repeatedly came on and the team's devices were activated.

She said: "I felt really uncomfortable down there.

"Anything lurking in the cellar isn't going to be good."

Two men who had previously worked at the mill also joined the investigation and, according to Emma, were unable to explain some of what was happening.

Inside the Bury Mill (Image: Emma Flood)

Experiences at the mill and another investigation in Bacup have even changed the way Emma and Lorna approach supposedly haunted locations.

Instead of always referring to spirits in the past tense, they have begun to wonder whether those they are attempting to contact might perceive things very differently.

Emma said: "Do they think we're the ones that are dead?

"To them, could it still be real life?"

There will be plenty more opportunities to put that idea to the test as Halloween approaches.

(Image: Emma Flood)

Para-Northern, which was established in 2017, is due to investigate the Greater Manchester Museum of Transport on October 2, having previously visited the venue.

A Masonic hall in Bolton is next on the list towards the end of October, followed by an old theatre in November.

For Emma, it is the combination of the unexplained and the history behind the buildings which keeps drawing her back.

She added: "Honestly, it's so fascinating."
